root_text:
Last week, it was the HMPV virus, now it’s the usual suspects: USD/INR, FII selling, US10Y, Brent, DXY. 

LA wildfires seem to be fueling bearish sentiment.

 Add budget uncertainty and Trump’s possible return, and fear spreads.

nodes.author: Normal_2610
nodes.text: Fatigue is visible across market caps. Bearish breakdowns are everywhere. Negativity is contagious, and panic is easy to spot. I find sign in December and exit from swing stock without loss but my portfolio was down 4.9% in long term what I hold

nodes.author: Normal_2610
nodes.text: Markets are always changing, and so am I. Staying invested through LTCG tax revisions, election results, and big market corrections paid off. Knowing what I own and why I own it helped me stay calm. Changing a strategy that worked seems foolish now. Familiar stocks with strong earnings make drawdowns easier to handle

nodes.author: Normal_2610
nodes.text: Bearish markets resemble wildfires—worse when deadwood piles up. Sharp falls won’t stop until weak hands exit. Social media accelerates fear like a virus. Market sentiment can be modeled like disease spread. Immunity builds up the same way. I might explore this concept more deeply in the future.

nodes.author: Normal_2610
nodes.text: It’s just two weeks into the year, and the market’s already shaky. My portfolio is now 11 stocks: Ceinsys, Shaily, Wockhardt, Axiscades, garware, laurus etc.,  7 are up, 4 are down. Ceinsys secured a ₹380 Cr order, Wockhardt’s drug trials look promising, Shaily’s exports are steady

nodes.author: Normal_2610
nodes.text: Axiscades surged but could be a value buy below ₹700. I’m unsure how long this bearish phase will last, but I expect 40–50% earnings growth in FY26 for these holdings. If things go wrong, at least I’ll know why I stayed put.
